translations.text: Before I formed you in the womb, I knew you, and before you came out of the womb, I made you holy. I appointed you as a prophet to many nations.
And the Lord stretched out his hand toward me and touched my mouth. And the Lord said to me, “Look, I have put my words in your mouth.”
Look, today I have appointed you over nations and kings, to uproot and tear down and destroy, and afterward to build and plant.
And the word of the Lord came to me, saying, “What do you see, Jeremiah?” I said, “I see a branch of a walnut tree.”
And the Lord said to me, “You have seen correctly, because I am watching over my words to carry them out.”
And the word of the Lord came to me a second time, saying, “What do you see?” I said, “A pot with a fire burning beneath it, and its face turned toward the north.”
Hear the word of the Lord, house of Jacob, and every family of the house of [?].
This is what the Lord says: “What sin did your ancestors find in me, that they went far away from me and followed [?]?”
The priests did not say, “Where is the law of God?” And those who handled the law did not know me.
I will still bring a case against you, and I will bring a case against your children’s children.
The heavens were disturbed by this, and the earth trembled greatly, says the Lord.
For my people have done two evil things: they have abandoned me, the spring of living water, and dug themselves broken cisterns that cannot hold water.
What have you to do with the road to Egypt, to drink the muddy water of the Gihon? And what have you to do with the road to Assyria, to drink water from their rivers?
Your disobedience will teach you, and your wickedness will rebuke you. Understand and see that it is bitter for you to abandon me. My goodwill has not rested upon you, says the Lord your God.
For long ago you broke your yoke and tore off your bonds. You said, “I will not serve.”
But I planted you as a fruitful vine, entirely true. How have you turned into bitterness, a vine that has become foreign?
Even if you wash yourself with washing soda and use plenty of soap, you have become deeply stained by injustice before me, says the Lord.
Look at your ways in the burial ground, and understand what you have done.
She went out, boasting in the desires of her soul.
Have I become a wilderness to the house of [?], or a land full of thorns? For my people have said, “There is no one who will rule over us, and from now on we will not come to you.”
Will a bride forget the ornaments she wears, or will a virgin forget the band tied around her? Yet my people have forgotten me for days beyond counting.
What good will you now do in your ways, to seek love? Was this not your desire? But you yourself acted wickedly, defiling yourself in your ways.
And on your hands they found the blood of innocent people. I did not find them in hidden places, but I found them upon every tall tree.
And you said, “I am innocent. Let your anger turn away from me.” Look, I will bring you to judgment because you say, “I have not sinned.”
[?] forever? Or will this be a victory for you? Look, you have spoken and done all these evil things, and you have prevailed.
And he did not turn back, and the community of Judah saw her disobedience.
Despite all these things, foolish Judah did not return to me with her whole heart, but only in falsehood.
And I will take you, one from a city and two from a clan, and bring you into Zion.
I will give you shepherds after my own heart, [?] shepherds who will tend you with instruction.

And when you multiply and increase on the earth in those days, says the Lord, they will no longer say, “The ark of the covenant of the Holy One [?].” It will not enter their minds, nor will they mention its name or look for it, and they will not make it again.

In those days, and during those days, they will call [?] “the throne of the Lord,” and all the nations will gather to her in the name of the Lord. They will no longer follow the desires of their evil hearts.

In those days the house of Judah and the house of [?] will come together. They will come together from the northern land and from all the countries into the land that I gave your ancestors to inherit.

I too said, “This will happen, Lord: I will place you among children and give you a choice land as an inheritance from God Almighty.” And I said, “You will call me ‘My Father,’ and you will not turn away from me.”
But just as a woman has been unfaithful to her husband, so the house of [?] has been unfaithful to me, says the Lord.
A voice was heard from lips: the weeping and pleading of the children of [?], because they have acted unjustly.
Return to me, children who have gone astray, and I will heal your wounds.
The prophet's astonishment.
And I said, “O Lord God, have you truly deceived this people and [?], saying, ‘You will have peace,’ while the sword has reached into their souls?”
The way of the daughter of my people is neither straight nor clean.
Wash their heart clean of wickedness, [?], so that you may be saved [?] thoughts of their suffering.
For the voice of the herald is coming from Dan, and they will hear anguish from the mountain of Ephraim.
Let the nations remember. Look!
Your ways and your deeds have brought these things upon you. This is your wickedness: it is bitter, and it has reached into your heart.
Suddenly the tent was devastated; my curtains were torn.
And they are not wise. They are skilled at doing evil, but they do not know how to do good.
I looked at the earth, and there was nothing; I looked up at heaven, and its lights were gone.
I saw the mountains, and they were trembling, and all the hills were shaking.
I looked, and there was no one, and all the birds of the sky had scattered.
I looked, and Carmel had become a wilderness. All the cities were burned before the Lord and destroyed before his fierce anger.
This is what the Lord says: “The whole earth will become a wilderness, but I will not destroy it.”
Because of these things, let the earth mourn and heaven grow dark, because I have spoken and will not change my mind. I have set my purpose on it and will not turn away from it.

At the sound of a horseman and a bow being drawn to shoot arrows, the whole earth was thrown into turmoil. The whole country withdrew. They went into their caves and hid in wooded places; they climbed up onto the rocks. Every city was abandoned, and no one lived in them.

And you, what will you do? Even if you put on scarlet clothes, adorn yourself with gold ornaments, and put eye paint on your eyes, your beautifying is useless, because your lovers have abandoned you. They will seek your life.

I heard their groaning like the voice of a woman in labor. The voice of the daughter of Zion was like the voice of a woman giving birth, about to faint and stretching out her hands: “Woe to me! My soul has collapsed because of those who were killed.”
Run through the streets of [?], look and understand, and search its squares. If you find a person who acts justly and seeks faithfulness, I will forgive them, says the Lord.
They say, “As the Lord lives.” Do they not, then, swear falsely?

Lord, your eyes look for faithfulness. You whipped them, but they felt no pain. You destroyed them, but they did not accept correction. They made their faces harder than rock and were unwilling to turn back.
I too said, “Perhaps they are poor, because they have been unable, because they have not known the way of the Lord or the judgment of God.”
But I will go to those who have power and speak with them, because they know the way of the Lord and the justice of God. Yet look, they too have all together broken the yoke and torn apart the bonds.

Because of this, a lion from the forest attacked them, and a wolf destroyed them as far as their houses. A leopard lay in wait outside their cities. Everyone who comes out of them will be seized, because they have multiplied their wicked deeds and grown strong in their rebellion.
Which of these things shall I forgive you for? Your children have abandoned me and swear by those who are not gods. I fed them, and they committed adultery and settled in prostitutes’ houses.
They became like stallions lusting after females, each one neighing for his neighbor’s wife.
“Shall I not call them to account for these things?” says the Lord. “Or shall my soul not take revenge on a nation like this?”
Go up onto her walls and tear them down.
Look, I have put my words in your mouth like fire, and this people like wood, so that it may consume them.
They do not see, and they have ears but do not hear.
“Will you not fear me?” says the Lord. “Or will you not tremble before me?” And they cannot cross it.
But this people acquired a disobedient and unbelieving heart. They turned away and went off.
They did not say in their hearts, “Let us fear the Lord our God, who gives us the early and the late rain.”
But your lawlessness has turned these things away from you, and your sins have caused good things to be far from you.
For wicked people were found among my people; they took their stand.
They violated justice. They did not judge the orphan’s case. [?] a widow [?] over these things [?].
My people loved it this way.
And sound a trumpet in Tekoa, and raise a signal over Beth-haccherem.
They will discipline you [?] with suffering and a scourge, lest my soul turn away from you and I make you a land where no one walks.

I have multiplied my anger; I have held it back. I will pour out my anger on the little children outside and on the gathering of young men together. A man and a woman will be seized, an old man and one who has reached the fullness of his days.
Look, I will bring disasters upon this people and upon the fruit of their disobedience, because they did not pay attention to my word and abandoned my law.
Why do you bring frankincense from Sheba and cinnamon from a distant land? Your burnt offerings are not acceptable, and your sacrifices do not please me.
Therefore, this is what the Lord says: “Look, I will bring a sickness upon this people, and fathers and children together will grow weak from it. A friend and his neighbor will perish.”
This is what the Lord says: “Look, a people is coming from the north, and a great nation will rise from the ends of the earth.”
And they hold a bow and a spear. He is cruel and will not show mercy.

Daughter of my people, put on sackcloth and sprinkle ashes on yourself. Make a lament and a great mourning, as though you had lost loved ones, for misery and a shadow are coming upon you suddenly and with turmoil.
Call them “Rejected [?],” because the Lord has rejected them.
[?] an orphan and a widow with violence. And do not shed innocent blood in this place, and do not follow foreign gods to your own harm.
I will let you live in this place, in the land that I gave to you and your ancestors, from everlasting to everlasting.
But if you have put your trust in lying words, these will bring you no benefit.
And you murder, commit adultery, swear falsely to support injustice, steal, and offer incense to Baal. You have followed foreign gods whom you do not know.
so that harm comes to you.
Their wives knead dough to make cakes for the army of heaven.
Gather together your burnt offerings and your sacrifices.
Shave your head. And he has rejected the generation that does these things.
They built the altar of Topheth, and [?] the valley of the son of Hinnom, to burn their sons and daughters in fire—something I did not command them to do and did not think of in my heart.
They will not be mourned or buried. They will be a spectacle on the face of the earth.
Does someone who falls not get up? Or does someone who turns away not turn back again?

Pay attention now, then, and do not listen to their words so casually. For there is no one who repents of his wickedness, saying, “What have I done?” The runner has stopped on his course, like a horse covered in sweat from its neighing.
The stork in the sky knows its place. The swallow, the dove, and the birds of the field observe their time for coming together.
Is the Lord not in Zion? Or is there no king there? Why have you angered me with your carved idols and those worthless foreign things?
I have mourned in sorrow over the crushing of the daughter of my people. Pains have overcome me like those of a woman about to give birth.
Is there, then, no balm in Gilead? Or is there no physician there? Why has healing not come to the daughter of my people?
Who will put water upon my head and a spring of tears upon my eyes, so that I may weep over this people day and night?
Who will give me a distant place to stay in the wilderness, so that I may leave this people behind and go far away from them? For they are all adulterers, an assembly of those who have broken faith.
Falsehood has prevailed on the earth, and not faithfulness.
Let everyone be on guard against his neighbor, and do not trust your brothers. For every brother will thoroughly deceive, and every friend will act deceitfully.
Everyone will mock his friend, and they will not speak the truth, for their tongues have learned to speak lies.
Therefore, this is what the Lord says: “Look, I will refine them and test them, for I will act in response to the wickedness of the daughter of my people.”
Their tongue is an arrow that wounds. The words of their mouths are deceitful. A person speaks peaceful words to his neighbor, but hostility is in his heart.
“Will I not punish them for these things?” says the Lord. “Or will my soul not take revenge on a people like this?”

Raise a lament over the mountains, and weep over the roads of the wilderness, for they have been abandoned because no one lives there. They have not heard the sound of those who live there. From the birds to the livestock, they have departed and perished.
I will turn [?] into a place of exile and a dwelling for the dragon. I will leave the cities of Judah in ruin, so that no one will live in them.
Call the women who lament, and let them come. Send for the skilled women, and let them open their mouths.
For death has come up through your windows.
In his wealth.

But let anyone who boasts boast in this: that he knows me and understands that I am the Lord, who practices mercy, justice, and righteousness on the earth. For these are the things I desire,” says the Lord.
Look, days are coming, says the Lord, when I will punish everyone who has been circumcised in their uncircumcision.

That is, Egypt, Idumea, Edom, the descendants of Ammon, the descendants of Moab, and everyone whose temples are shaved, those who live in the wilderness. For all the nations are uncircumcised in their flesh, but the house of [?] is uncircumcised in heart.
Listen to the word that the Lord has spoken against you, house of [?].
This is what the Lord says: Do not follow the ways of the nations, and do not be afraid of the signs in the sky, because the nations are afraid of them as they watch them.
For the customs of the nations are worthless. It is a tree cut down in a forest, the work of a carpenter, and their gods are material that has been cast.
They decorate them with silver and gold, fastening them with nails and hammers so that they will not move.
They are beaten silver, and they cannot walk. They must be carried because they cannot walk. Do not be afraid of them, because they cannot do any harm, and there is no good in them.
There is silver from Tarshish in them, and gold from Mophaz, and the work of a goldsmith’s hand. They are all the work of craftsmen, who dress them in blue and purple.
This is what you are to say to them: Let the gods that did not make the sky and the earth perish from the earth and from beneath the sky.
The Lord is the one who made the sky and the earth by his power, who established the inhabited world by his wisdom, and who spread out the sky by his understanding.
He placed abundant water in the sky, bringing clouds up from the ends of the earth. He made his lightning for the rain, and brought the winds out of their storehouses.
Everyone has become foolish, without knowledge. Every goldsmith has been put to shame by his carved images, because they cast them in falsehood, and there is no [?] within them.
For they are worthless works, works of mockery. They will perish at the time when they are punished.
But Jacob’s portion is not like these, because he is the one who formed everything. He is his inheritance. The Lord of hosts is his name.
He brought out your possessions, which are kept in the chosen places.
For this is what the Lord says: Look, I myself will strike down those who live in this land with distress, so that your wound [?].
Correct us, Lord, but with justice, not in your anger, so that you do not reduce us to nothing.
Pour out your wrath on the nations that have not known you, and on the kingdoms that have not called on your name.
Why has my beloved committed abominations in my house?

The Lord called you an olive tree, beautiful to look at and giving shade. At the sound of its pruning, however, a fire has now blazed up over it. Great is the distress upon you; its branches have become useless.
Lord, make it known to me, and I will understand. Then I saw their deeds.

But I was like an innocent lamb being taken to slaughter. I did not know that they had plotted an evil scheme against me, saying, ‘Come, let us put wood into his bread and remove him from the land of the living, so that his name will no longer be remembered.’
Lord of hosts, who judges justly and examines hearts and kidneys, let me see the vengeance you will take on them, because I have revealed my innocence to you.
Therefore this is what the Lord says about the people of Anathoth who seek your life and say, ‘Do not prophesy to us in the Lord’s name, or you will die at our hands.’
Look, I myself will punish them. Their young men will fall by the sword, and their sons and daughters will die of hunger.
And no survivors will remain among them, because I will bring disasters upon those who live in Anathoth in the year when I call them to account.

You are righteous, Lord; therefore I will speak before you. Still, I will present matters of justice to you. Why does the way of the ungodly prosper? Why do all those who act treacherously flourish in their disobedience?
You planted them, and they put down roots. They produced offspring and bore fruit. You are near them in their mouths, but far from their hearts.
But you, Lord, know me. You have seen me and tested my heart before you. Set them apart, then, for the day of their slaughter.

How long will the land mourn and all the grass of the field dry up? Because of the wickedness of those who live on the land, they have destroyed the animals and the birds. They said, “God will not see our ways.”
Your feet run, and they wear you out. How will you be able to prepare yourself to compete with horses? You have put your confidence in a peaceful land; what will you do in the swelling of the Jordan?
For your brothers and your father's household—they too have betrayed you. They became afraid and gathered together behind your back. Do not trust them, even though they speak good things to you.
I abandoned my house; I abandoned my inheritance. I handed my beloved soul over to her enemies.
My inheritance became to me like a lion in the forest. In this way she raised her voice against me; therefore I hated her.
Is my inheritance a hyena's den to me, or is there a cave around her? Go and gather all the wild animals of the field. Let them come to devour her.
Many shepherds have destroyed my vineyard and defiled my portion. They have turned my choice portion into a wilderness where no one walks.
They have made it a ruined wasteland because of me. The whole land has been utterly ruined, because no one takes it to heart.
They came in misery across the whole expanse of the wilderness, for the Lord's sword will devour from one end of the land to the other. There is no peace for any living person.
Sow wheat and reap thorns. Their allotted portions will not benefit them. Be ashamed of your boasting and your anger before the Lord.
For this is what the Lord says about all the wicked neighbors who lay hands on my inheritance, which I allotted to my people: [?] Look, I will uproot them from their land, and the house of Judah [?]
This is what the Lord says: “Go and get yourself a cloth loincloth and wrap it around your waist.”
And take that loincloth which I commanded you to hide in that place.
And I went to the Euphrates River, dug, and took the loincloth out of the place where I had buried it. And look, it had rotted and was no longer good for anything.
The word of the Lord came to me, saying, “This is what the Lord says:
In this way I will destroy the pride of Judah and the great pride of [?]
Those who did not want to listen to my words, but went and followed foreign gods to serve them and worship them, will become like this loincloth, which is no longer useful for anything.
For just as a loincloth clings to a person's waist, so I made the house of [?] and the whole house of Judah cling to me, so that they would be my people, bringing fame, praise, and glory.
A man and his brother, their fathers and their children together, says the Lord. I will not love them, nor will I spare them, nor will I have compassion over their destruction.
Listen and pay attention. Do not exalt yourselves, for the Lord has spoken.
Give glory to the Lord your God before darkness comes and before his feet stumble on the dark mountains. You will look for light, but the shadow of death is there, and they will be left in darkness.
But if you do not listen, your soul will weep in secret because of your pride, and your eyes will pour down tears, because the Lord's flock has been broken.
Tell the king and the powerful, “Humble yourselves and sit down, because the crown of your glory has been taken from your heads.”
The cities in the south have been shut, and there is no one to open them. Judah has been taken into exile, undergoing a complete and great exile.
Lift up your eyes, [?], and look at those coming from the north. Where is the flock that was given to you, the sheep of your glory?
What will you say when they come to inspect you? You taught them lessons so that they would rise up against you from the beginning. Will pains not seize you like a woman about to give birth?
And if you say in their heart, “Why have these things happened to me?” it is because of their many injustices that their backsides have been uncovered and their heels exposed.
If an Ethiopian can change the color of his body, and a leopard can clean away its spots, then you too can do good, although you have been taught to do evil.
And I scattered them like chaff that the wind carries into the wilderness.
This is your lot, and this is your portion for your lack of faith in me, says the Lord, since you forgot me and put your hope in lies.
I too will uncover their backsides and bring them before you, and their shame will be revealed,

along with the estrangement of their prostitution, their adultery, and their neighing. I saw their abominations on the hills and in the fields. Woe to you, Jerusalem, because you have not been cleansed so as to follow me! How long will this continue?
The word of the Lord came to Jeremiah because no rain had fallen.
Judea mourned, and her gates became empty. They grew dark upon the ground, and the cry of Jerusalem went up.
And her nobles sent their young servants to get water. They came to the cisterns but found none, and they brought their vessels back empty.
Work on the land ceased because no rain had fallen. The farmers were ashamed and covered their heads.
The deer gave birth in the field and abandoned their young because there was no vegetation for them to eat.
The wild donkeys stood in the wooded places and drew in the wind. Their eyes failed because there was no grass for them.
Even if our sins stand against us, Lord, act for us for the sake of your name, because our sins before you are many, for we have sinned against you.
Lord, you are the hope of Israel; you save us in times of trouble. Why have you become like a stranger in the land, and like a villager who has turned aside to a lodging place?
Will you be like a forgetful man, or like a man who has no power to save? Yet you, Lord, are among us, and your name has been proclaimed over us. Do not forget us.
This is what the Lord says to this people: “They loved to move their feet and did not restrain them. God took no pleasure in them. Now, therefore, he will remember their injustices.”
And the Lord said to me, “Do not pray for the welfare of this people,
for if they fast, I will not listen to their plea, and if they bring burnt offerings and sacrifices, I will not take pleasure in them. For I will destroy them by sword, famine, and death.”

And I said, “Lord, the One who is, look: their prophets are prophesying and saying, ‘You will not see the sword, nor will famine come among you, for I will give truth and peace in this land and in this place.’”

And the Lord said to me, “These prophets are prophesying lies in my name. I did not send them, nor did I command them, nor did I speak with them. They are prophesying to you false visions, divinations, omens, and the desires of their own hearts.

Therefore, this is what the Lord says about the prophets who prophesy lies in my name, although I did not send them, saying, ‘Neither sword nor famine will come upon this land’: These prophets will perish through deadly disease and will be destroyed by famine,

along with the people to whom they prophesy. They will lie thrown into the streets of Jerusalem because of the sword and famine, with no one to bury them, their wives, or their children. I will pour their evil deeds upon them.

And you shall tell them this word: ‘Let your eyes pour down tears day and night, and do not let them stop flowing, because the daughter of my people has been shattered and struck with a very painful wound.’
If I go out into the field, there are people killed by the sword; and if I go into the city, there is the suffering of famine. For prophet and priest alike have gone to a land they do not know.
Have you completely rejected Judah? Has your soul turned away from Zion? Why have you afflicted us, with no healing for us? We waited for peace, and
Even if Moses and Samuel stood before me, I would not forgive them.
the wild animals of the earth, to eat them and destroy them.
I will hand them over to distress under all the kings of the earth because of Manasseh son of Hezekiah, king of Judah, because of everything he did in [?].
Who will have pity on you, [?]? Who will mourn over you? Or who will turn aside to greet you?
You have turned away from me, says the Lord. You will go backward, and I will stretch out my hand against you and wipe you out. I will no longer forgive them.
I will winnow them with a winnowing fan out of the gates of my people. I have become childless; I have destroyed my people because of their acts of violence.
Their widows have become more numerous than the sand of the sea. I brought misery upon the mother of a young man at noon. I suddenly cast trembling and turmoil upon her.

The woman who bore seven children has become childless. Her soul has fainted. The sun set on her while it was still midday. She was put to shame and mocked. I will hand over those who remain of them to the sword before the Lord.

Woe to me, my mother! You gave birth to me as a man whom people judge and dispute with throughout the whole land. I have not taken interest, and no one has paid me interest. My strength has failed among those who curse me.
May this happen to me, says the Lord, when they prosper, if I did not stand before you on their behalf in the time of their troubles and in the time of their distress, for their good before the Lord.
Can they recognize iron? Your strength is covered like bronze.
And I will give your treasures over to plunder without payment, because of all the sins you committed throughout all your territories.
And I will make you a slave in the hands of your enemies, in a land you do not know. For a fire has been kindled in my anger; it will burn against you.
Lord, remember me, look after me, and rescue me from those who pursue me. Do not delay. Know how I have suffered reproach for your sake.
Because of those who reject your words, wipe them out. Your word will bring me gladness and joy in my heart, because your name has been called over me, Lord Almighty.
I did not sit in their assembly as they laughed. Instead, I was afraid before your hand. I sat apart, alone, because I was filled with bitterness.
Why do those who cause me anguish overpower me? My wound is severe. How will I recover? It has indeed become for me like deceptive water with no fear in it.
Therefore, this is what the Lord says: If you turn back, I will establish you, and you will stand before me. And if you bring forth what is precious
They will not be mourned or buried. They will become an example on the face of the earth.
Look, I will put an end in this place, before your eyes and in your days, to the sound of gladness and the sound of joy, the voice of a bridegroom and the voice of a bride.
And when you tell this people all these words, they will say to you, 'Why has the Lord [?]? What is the sin we have committed before the Lord our God?'
And you will tell them, 'Because your ancestors abandoned me, says the Lord, and followed foreign gods, served them, and worshiped them. I
You yourselves have acted more wickedly than your ancestors. Look, each of you follows the desires of your evil heart, so that you do not listen to me.
And I will cast you out of this land into a land that neither you nor your ancestors know, and you will serve foreign gods who will show you no mercy.
Therefore, look, days are coming, says the Lord, when they will no longer say, “As the Lord lives, who brought the children of [?] out of the land of Egypt.”
Instead, they will say, “As the Lord lives, who brought the house of [?] out.” And I will restore them to their land, which I gave to their ancestors.
Look, I will send many fishermen, says the Lord, and they will catch them. After this I will send many hunters, and they will hunt them, even out of the clefts in the rocks.
For my eyes watch all their ways, and their injustices have not been hidden from my eyes.
And I will repay them double for their injustices and their sins, with which they defiled my land, through the lawless deeds they committed in my inheritance.

Lord, you are my strength and my help, and my refuge on the day of trouble. The nations will come to you from the ends of the earth and say before you, “Surely the idols our ancestors acquired for themselves are lies, and there is no benefit in them.”
Can a person make gods for himself? Yet these are not gods.
Therefore, look, this time I will make them know my hand, and I will make them know my strength, and they will understand that my name is the Lord.
Cursed is the person whose hope rests on a human being, who relies on the flesh of his arm, and who turns his heart away from the Lord.
He will be like a male donkey in the wilderness. He will not see good things when they come, but will live in parched places in the wilderness, in a salty land where no one lives.
But blessed is the person who has put his trust in the Lord, and the Lord will be his hope.

He will be like a tree growing beside water, sending its roots out beside a stream. It will not be afraid when heat comes upon it. It will have branches with abundant leaves, and it will not be afraid if the rain fails to come for a year, nor will it cease bearing fruit.
His heart is more remarkable than anything, and he is a human being. Who, then, will know him?
I am the Lord who searches hearts and tests kidneys, to give each person according to his ways, and according to his ways, and according to the fruit of his deeds.
The partridge is a bird: it called out and gathered together young that it had not produced.

This is what the Lord says: “Go and stand at the gates of the children of your people, through which the kings of Judah enter and through which they also leave. Stand also at all the other gates of Jerusalem.”
And you shall say to them, “Hear the word of the Lord, kings of Judah, all Judea, and all Jerusalem, you who enter through these gates.”
This is what the Lord says: “Guard your lives, and do not carry a load on Sabbath days or bring it through the gates of Jerusalem.”
“And do not bring a load out of your houses on the Sabbath day, and do not do any work. Keep the Sabbath day holy, as I commanded your ancestors. But they did not listen or incline their ears.”
They made their necks stiffer than their ancestors’ necks, refusing to listen to me or accept instruction.
And it will happen, if you listen to me, says the Lord, that you will bring no loads through the gates of this city on the Sabbath day, do no work, and keep the Sabbath day holy.
Kings and rulers sitting on David’s throne will enter through the gates of this city.
Or will water flowing forcefully be scattered, with a wind behind it?

Instead, each person will die for their own sin, and whoever eats sour grapes will have their own teeth set on edge.
“Look, days are coming,” says the Lord, “when I will establish a new covenant with the house of [?] and the house of Judah.”

“It will not be like the covenant I established with their fathers on the day I took them by the hand to bring them out of the land of Egypt. They did not remain in my covenant, and I, in turn, disregarded them,” says the Lord.
“For this is the covenant I will establish with the house of [?] after those days: I will surely put my laws upon [?]”
Babylon surrounded [?], and Jeremiah was being held under guard in the prison courtyard in the king’s house.

This was the place where King Zedekiah had imprisoned him, saying: Why do you prophesy, saying, ‘This is what the Lord says: Look, I will hand this city over to the king of Babylon, and he will capture it’?
“Zedekiah will not escape from the hand of the Chaldeans, for he will surely be handed over to the king of Babylon. He will speak with him mouth to mouth and see him eye to eye.”
“Zedekiah will go down to Babylon and remain there.”
The word of the Lord came to Jeremiah, saying:
“Look, Hanamel, the son of Shallum, your father’s brother, is coming to you, saying, ‘Buy the field in Anathoth for yourself, for you have the legal right to acquire it by purchase.’”

And Hanamel, the son of Shallum, my father's brother, came to me in the prison courtyard. He said to me, “Buy my field in Anathoth, in the land of Benjamin, because you have the right to acquire it, since you are the eldest.” And I knew that this was the word of the Lord.
I bought the field from Hanamel, the son of my father's brother, and weighed out seventeen shekels of silver for him.
And I wrote a document and sealed it. I had witnesses testify, and I weighed the silver on a balance.
And I took the deed of sale, the sealed one and the one that had been read.

I gave it to Baruch, the son of Neriah, the son of Maaseiah, in the presence of Hanamel, the son of my father's brother, and in the presence of those standing there who had signed the deed of sale, and in the presence of the Jews sitting in the prison courtyard.
And I gave Baruch instructions in their presence, saying to him:
This is what the Lord Almighty said: “Take this deed of sale, the document that has been read, and put it in an earthenware vessel so that it may last for many days.”
For this is what the Lord said: “Fields, houses, and vineyards will again be acquired in this land.”
And after giving the document to Baruch, the son of Neriah, I prayed to the Lord, saying:
“O Lord, you who exist, you made heaven and earth by your great power and your uplifted arm. Nothing can be hidden from you.
You show mercy to thousands and repay the sins of the fathers into the laps of their children after them, O great and mighty God,
the Lord of great counsel, mighty in his works, God Almighty, the Lord whose name is great. Your eyes watch the ways of human beings, so that you may give each one according to his way.
You have performed signs and wonders in the land of Egypt down to this day, and among [?] and the peoples of the earth. You have made a name for yourself, as it is today.
And you brought your people, [?], out of the land of Egypt with signs and wonders, with a mighty hand and an uplifted arm,
and with great terrors. And you gave them this land, which you swore to their fathers to give them, a land flowing with milk and honey.
They entered it and took possession of it.
[?] anger me—they, their kings, their rulers, and their [?].
which is in the valley of the son of Hinnom, so that they might give [?]
to the king of Babylon, by the sword, famine, and [?]
throughout all their days, [?] what is good for them and their children
upon this people all these great disasters, so I too will bring upon them all the good things that I said I would bring upon them.
And they will again acquire fields for themselves in this city, about which you say, ‘It will become a wasteland, with no one living in it, because it has been handed over to the Chaldeans.’

They will buy fields for silver, and you will write a document, seal it, and have witnesses testify, in the land of Benjamin and around [?], and in the towns of Judah, the towns of the hill country and the Shephelah, and the towns of the Negev. For I will bring back those who were deported, and [?]
And the word of the Lord came to Jeremiah a second time, while he was still confined in the prison courtyard, saying to him:
“This is what the Lord said, the one who makes the earth and forms it to establish it—the Lord is his name:
Call out to me, and I will answer you and tell you great things and mighty deeds that you have not known.”
For this is what the Lord said about the houses of this city and the houses of the king of Judah that were torn down
to make places for fighting the Chaldeans and to fill it with dead people whom I struck down in my anger and my fury. I turned my face away from them because of all their sexual immorality.
Look, I will bring healing upon it, reveal it, and treat it with peace and faithfulness.
And I will bring back the exiles of Judah and the exiles of [?], and rebuild them as before.
And I will cleanse them of all their acts of injustice through which they sinned against me. I will not remember the sins they committed against me when they turned away from me.

And it will become a joy, a blessing, and a source of greatness for all the people of the earth who will hear about all the good things I will do. They will be afraid and angry because of all the good things and all the peace I will give them.

This is what the Lord says: In this place, which you say is a wasteland with neither people nor animals, in the cities of Judah and outside Jerusalem, which have become desolate, with neither people nor animals living there, people will once again hear:

A sound of gladness and a sound of joy, the voice of the bridegroom and the voice of the bride, the voices of those who say, “Give thanks to the Lord Almighty, for the Lord is good, and his mercy lasts forever.” They will bring gifts into the house of the Lord, for I will bring back all the exiles of that land as before, says the Lord.
This is what the Lord of hosts says: In this deserted place and in all its cities, people will once again hear of shepherds’ sheepfolds, where they settle their flocks.

In the towns of the hill country, in the towns of the Shephelah, in the towns of the Negev and the land of Benjamin, in the towns around Jerusalem, and in the towns of Judah, sheep will again pass through the hands of the one who counts them, says the Lord.

The word that came to Jeremiah from the Lord when Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, and his whole army, all the land under his rule, and all the peoples were fighting against Jerusalem and all the towns of Judah, saying:

“This is what the Lord said: Go to Zedekiah, king of Judah, and tell him, ‘This is what the Lord said: This city will certainly be handed over to the king of Babylon. He will capture it and burn it with fire.
And you will not escape his hands. You will certainly be captured and handed over to him. Your eyes will see his eyes, and your mouth will speak with his mouth, and you will go into Babylon.
But listen to the word of the Lord, Zedekiah, king of Judah. This is what the Lord said:

You will die in peace. Just as they mourned your ancestors who reigned before you, so they will mourn you too and lament for you down to the realm of the dead. For I myself have spoken this word, says the Lord.
And Jeremiah spoke all these words to King Zedekiah in Jerusalem.
And the army of the king of Babylon was fighting against Jerusalem and against the towns of Judah, Lachish and Azekah, because these were the large towns that remained among the towns of Judah.
The word that came to Jeremiah from the Lord after King Zedekiah made a covenant with the people in Jerusalem to proclaim release,
so that each person would release his Hebrew male slave and his Hebrew female slave, setting them free, so that no one from Judah would be enslaved.
And all the officials and all the people who had entered the covenant turned back, so that each would release his male slave and each his female slave.
And they were keeping them as slaves.
The word of the Lord came to Jeremiah, saying:
For this is what the Lord says: I made a covenant with your ancestors on the day I rescued them from the land of Egypt, from the house of their slavery, saying to them:

“When six years have been completed, you must release your fellow Hebrew who is handed over to you. He will work for you for six years, and you must release him as a free person. But your ancestors did not listen to me or turn their ears toward me.
Today they turned back to do what is right in my sight, each one granting freedom to his neighbor. They made a covenant before me in the house that bears my name.
And you turned back and defiled my name by each of you taking back his male slave and his female slave, whom you had released to live freely as they wished. You made them your slaves again.

Therefore this is what the Lord said: You did not listen to me by each granting release to his neighbor. Look, I will send you a release, says the Lord—to the sword, death, and famine. And I will scatter you throughout all the kingdoms of the earth.”
And I will hand over the men who abandoned my covenant, who did not uphold my covenant, but made before me the calf that they made to work with [?]—
the rulers of Judah, the powerful men, the priests, and the people.
I will hand them over to their enemies, and their killers will become food for the birds of the sky and the wild animals of the earth.
And Zedekiah, king of Judea, and their rulers—I will hand them over to their enemies and to the army of the king of Babylon, from whom they are fleeing.

Look, I am giving the command, says the Lord. I will bring them back to this city, and they will fight against it, capture it, and burn it with fire, along with the cities of Judah. I will make them a wasteland, with no one living in them.
The word that came to Jeremiah from the Lord in the days of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah, saying:
“Go into the house of the Rechabites and call them. Bring them into the house of the Lord, into one of the courtyards, and give them wine to drink there.”
And I brought out Jaazaniah son of Jeremiah, son of Habazziniah, along with his brothers, his sons, and the whole household of the Rechabites.

I brought them into the house of the Lord, into the chamber of Johanan son of Hananiah, the man of God. It was beside the chamber of the officials, above the chamber of Maaseiah son of Shallum, the keeper of the courtyard.
And I set a jug of wine and cups before them and said to them, “Drink wine.”
They said, “We will not drink wine, because our ancestor Jonadab son of Rechab commanded us, saying, ‘You and your children must never drink wine.
And you must not build a house or sow seed, and you must not have vineyards. Instead, you must live in tents all your days, so that you may live a long time on the land where you reside.’
And we obeyed our ancestor Jonadab in everything he commanded us: not to drink wine all our days—we, our wives, our sons, and our daughters—
and not to build a house to live in. And we have had no vineyard, field, or seed.
Instead, we have lived in tents, and we have obeyed and done everything our ancestor Jonadab commanded us.

But when Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, came against the land, they said, ‘Come into the city.’ And we went into Jerusalem because of the army of the Chaldeans and the army of the Assyrians, and we settled there.”
The word of the Lord came to me, saying:
For this is what the Lord says: “Go and say to the people of Judah and those living in Jerusalem, ‘Will you not accept instruction and obey my words?
The descendants of Jonadab son of Rechab have upheld the command their ancestor gave them not to drink wine, and they have not drunk it. But I spoke to you early; I spoke, and you did not listen.

I sent you my servants the prophets, saying, “Let each of you turn away from your evil ways, and let your deeds improve. Do not follow other gods and serve them, so that you may live on the land I gave you and your ancestors.” But you did not turn your ears toward me or listen to me.
The descendants of Jonadab have upheld their ancestor’s command, which he gave them, but these people have not obeyed me.
Therefore, this is what the Lord said: “Look, I will bring upon Judah and those living in Jerusalem the disasters that I said I would bring upon them.”
Therefore, this is what the Lord said: “Since the descendants of Jonadab son of Rechab obeyed their ancestor’s command, doing as their ancestor commanded them—
The descendants of Jonadab son of Rechab will never lack a man to stand before me throughout all the days of the earth.
In the fourth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah, the word of the Lord came to me, saying:

“Take a scroll of papyrus and write on it all these words that I spoke to you concerning Jerusalem and Judah and all the nations, from the day I spoke to you, from the days of Josiah, king of Judah, up to this very day.”
Perhaps the house of Judah will hear about all these disasters that I plan to bring upon them, so that they turn away from their evil way, and I will forgive their injustices and their sins.
Jeremiah called Baruch son of Neriah, and Baruch wrote on a scroll, at Jeremiah’s dictation, all the words of the Lord that he had spoken to him.
Jeremiah instructed Baruch, saying, “I am under guard and cannot enter the Lord’s house.
You go in and read this scroll aloud to the people in the Lord’s house on the day of fasting. You must also read it aloud to all the people of Judah who come from their towns.”
Perhaps mercy will come upon them in the Lord’s presence, and they will turn away from their evil way, for great are the anger and wrath that the Lord has declared against this people.
Baruch did everything Jeremiah had instructed him to do, reading the words of the Lord from the scroll in the Lord’s house.
In the eighth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah, in the ninth month, all the people in Jerusalem and the house of Judah gathered to observe a fast before the Lord.

Baruch read the scroll containing Jeremiah’s words in the Lord’s house, in the room of Gemariah son of Shaphan the scribe, in the upper courtyard, by the entrance to the New Gate of the Lord’s house, so that all the people could hear.
Micaiah son of Gemariah, son of Shaphan, heard all the words of the Lord from the scroll.

He went down to the king’s house, to the scribe’s room. There all the officials were sitting: Elishama the scribe, Delaiah son of Shelemiah, Jonathan son of Achbor, Gemariah son of Shaphan, Zedekiah son of Hananiah, and all the officials.
Micaiah told them all the words he had heard while Baruch was reading the scroll aloud to the people.

All the officials sent word to Baruch son of Neriah, son of Athaniah, son of Shelemiah, son of Cushi, saying to him, “Take in your hand the scroll from which you are reading aloud to the people, and come.” Baruch son of Neriah took the scroll in his hand and went down to them.
They said to him, “Read these words aloud to us too.” And Baruch read.
When they heard all the words, they all consulted with one another, each with the person beside him. They said, “We must certainly tell the king all these words.”
They questioned Baruch, saying, “Where did you get all these words that you wrote?”
Baruch said to them, “Jeremiah dictated all these words to me himself, and I wrote them on this scroll.”
They said to Baruch, “Go and hide, you and Jeremiah. Do not let anyone know where you are.”
They went to the king in the courtyard, leaving the scroll for safekeeping in Elisha’s room, and told the king all these words.
The king sent Jehudi to fetch the scroll. He took it from Elisha’s room, and Jehudi read it aloud to the king and to all the officials standing around the king.
The king was sitting in a cold winter room, with burning coals in front of him.
As Jehudi read the third and fourth columns, he cut them off with the scribe’s knife and threw them onto the burning coals, until the entire scroll was consumed.
Neither the king nor his servants who heard all these words made any inquiry or tore their clothes.
Elnathan and Gedaliah told the king to burn the entire scroll.
The king ordered Jerahmeel, the king’s son, and Seraiah son of Azriel to seize Baruch and Jeremiah, but they hid themselves.
The word of the Lord came to Jeremiah after the king had burned the scroll containing all the words Baruch had written at Jeremiah’s dictation, saying to him:
“Take another scroll and write on it all these words that were in the scroll that King Jehoiakim burned.”

And you shall tell him, “This is what the Lord said: You burned this scroll, saying, ‘Why did you write in it that the king of Babylon will certainly come and destroy this land and remove people and animals from it?’”

Therefore this is what the Lord said about Jehoiakim, king of Judah: “None of his descendants will sit on David’s throne, and his corpse will lie exposed to the heat of the day and the cold of the night.

And I will punish him, his descendants, and his servants. I will bring upon him, his servants, the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and Judea all the disasters that I announced to them, but they did not listen.”
And Jeremiah took another scroll and gave it to Baruch. He wrote on it, at Jeremiah’s dictation, all the words of the scroll that Jehoiakim had burned. And he added many more words like them.
And Zedekiah son of Josiah became king in place of Jehoiakim. Nebuchadnezzar had made him king over Judah.
Neither he nor his servants nor the people of the land listened to the words of the Lord that he had spoken through Jeremiah.
And King Zedekiah sent Jucal son of Shelemiah and the priest Zephaniah son of Maaseiah to Jeremiah, saying, “Pray for us before the Lord.”
And Jeremiah came and went out from the midst of the city, and they had not put him in prison.
And Pharaoh’s army came out of Egypt. The Chaldeans heard of their arrival and withdrew from their position against Jerusalem.
The word of the Lord came to Jeremiah, saying to him:
This is what the Lord said: “This is what you must say to the king of Judah, who sent you to inquire of me: Look, Pharaoh’s army, which came to help you, will return to the land of Egypt.”
“And the Chaldeans will come and fight against this city, capture it, and burn it with fire.”
“This is what the Lord said: Do not think to yourselves, saying, ‘The Chaldeans will flee and leave us alone.’ Know, then, that they will not go away.
And even if you strike down the whole Chaldean army that is fighting against you, and some of them remain, each wounded in his own place, they will rise and burn this city with fire.”
And it happened, when the Chaldean army withdrew from Jerusalem before Pharaoh’s army,
that Jeremiah went out of Jerusalem to go to the land of Benjamin and stay there among the people.

And when he reached the Benjamin Gate, there was a man there who lay in wait for him. His name was Irijah son of Shelemiah, son of Hananiah. He seized Jeremiah, saying to him, “You are deserting to the Chaldeans!”
But Jeremiah said to him, “You are lying! I am not deserting to the Chaldeans.” But he did not listen to him. And Irijah seized Jeremiah and took him to the officials.
And the officials became angry with Jeremiah, beat him, and sent him to the house of Jonathan the scribe, because they had made his house into a prison.
And when Jeremiah entered the dungeon and went down into the cells, he stayed there for many days.
King Zedekiah sent for him and summoned him secretly. He questioned him, saying, “Do you have a word from the Lord?” Jeremiah said, “Yes. You will be handed over to the king of Babylon.”
And Jeremiah said to the king, “What wrong have I done to you, your servants, or your people, that you are throwing me into prison?
Where, then, are your prophets who prophesied to you, saying, ‘The king of Babylon will not come against this land’?
Now, then, my lord the king, let me find mercy in your presence. And why would you send me back down to the house of Jonathan the scribe, so that I die there?”

The king gave orders, and they put him in the prison. He gave him one loaf of bread each day, from outside, from the batch of bread they baked daily, until the bread in the city ran out. And Jeremiah stayed in the courtyard of the prison.
Now Zephaniah son of Nathan, Gedaliah son of Pashhur, and Jucal son of Shelemiah heard the words that Jeremiah spoke to the people, saying:
For this is what the Lord said: “Whoever remains in this city will die by the sword and by hunger, but whoever goes out to the Chaldeans will be saved. He will gain his life as a prize and survive.”
For this is what the Lord said: “This city will certainly be handed over to the army of the king of Babylon, and he will capture it.”

And they said to the king, “Let that man be killed, because he is weakening the hands of the fighting men who remain in the city, and the hands of all the people, by speaking these words to them. This man does not speak good words for the peace of this people, but speaks evil things against them.”
The king said to them, “Look, he is in your hands,” because the king could not prevail against them.

And they threw him down into the cistern of Malchiah, the king’s son, which was in the prison courtyard. And he lowered him into the cistern. There was no water in the cistern, only mud, and he was down in the mud.
Ebed-melech the Ethiopian, who was in the king’s house, heard that they had thrown Jeremiah into the cistern. The king was in the courtyard of Benjamin.
And Ebed-Melech came out and spoke to the king, saying to him,
“You have done evil in what you have done, causing the man of God to die of hunger, for there is now no bread in the city.”
And the king commanded Ebed-Melech, saying to him, “Take thirty men with you from here and bring him up out of the cistern, so that he does not die.”
And Ebed-Melech took the men and went into the lower part of the king’s house. He took worn cloth rags from there, along with ropes made of rags, and threw them down to Jeremiah in the cistern.
He said to him, “Put these underneath the ropes.” And Jeremiah did so.
They pulled him up with the ropes and brought him up out of the cistern. And Jeremiah stayed in the prison courtyard.
King Zedekiah sent for him and summoned him to the third house of Salisiel, which was in the house of the Lord. The king said to him, “I am asking you about something. Hide nothing from me.”
Jeremiah said to the king, “If I tell you, [?] you will put me to death. And if I give you advice, you will not listen to me.”
The king swore to him, saying, “As the Lord lives, who made this life for us, I will not kill you, and I will not hand you over to these men.”

And Jeremiah said to him, “This is what the Lord said: ‘If you go out to the commanders of the king of Babylon, your life will be spared, and this city will not be burned with fire. You and your household will live.’
“But if you do not go out, this city will be handed over to the Chaldeans, and they will burn it with fire, and you will not be saved.”
The king said to Jeremiah, “I have a concern about the Jews who fled to the Chaldeans: they might hand me over to them, and they might mock me.”
Jeremiah said to him, “They will not hand you over. Listen to the word of the Lord that I am telling you, and things will go well for you, and your life will be spared.
“But if you are unwilling to go out, this is the word that the Lord revealed to me:

“‘Look, all the women who remain in the house of the king of Judah will be brought out to the officials of the king of Babylon. These women were saying, “Your trusted friends have deceived you, and they will overpower you and cause your feet to slip.”’

“I have turned your wives away from you. Your children will be brought out to the Chaldeans, and you will not escape, for you will be captured by the king of Babylon, and this city will be burned with fire.”
And the king said to him, “Do not let anyone know about these words, and you will not die.

“But if the officials hear that I have spoken with you, and they come to you and say to you, ‘Tell us what the king said to you. Do not hide it from us, and we will not kill you. What did the king say to you?’
“You are to say to them, ‘I was pleading for mercy before the king, asking him not to send me back to Jonathan’s house to die there.’”
All the officials came to Jeremiah and questioned him. He told them everything the king had instructed him to say. So they remained silent, because they had not heard any word from him.
Jeremiah stayed in the prison courtyard until the time when Jerusalem was captured.
In the ninth month of Zedekiah, king of Judah, Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, came against Jerusalem with his entire army, and they surrounded it.
In the eleventh year of Zedekiah, in the fourth month, on the ninth day of the month, the city was breached.

All the officials of the king of Babylon entered it and sat at the middle gate. These were Marganasar, Samagoth, Nabusachar, Nabusaris, Nagargasnaser, Rab-mag, and the rest of the officials of the king of Babylon.
They sent for Jeremiah and took him out of the courtyard of the prison. They handed him over to Gedaliah son of Ahikam, son of Shaphan, and brought him out of the house. He lived among the people.
The word of the Lord came to Jeremiah in the courtyard of the prison, saying:
“Go and tell Ebed-melech the Ethiopian, ‘This is what the Lord, the God of [?], says: Look, I will bring my words upon this city for harm and not for good.
I will rescue you on that day and will not hand you over to the men you fear.
For I will certainly save you, and you will not fall by the sword. Your life will be your gain, because you have put your trust in me, says the Lord.’”

The word that came to Jeremiah from the Lord after Nebuzaradan, the captain of the guard, sent him away from Daman [?], when he took him in bronze chains among the exiles of Judah, from their governors [?], down to Babylon.
The captain of the guard took Jeremiah and said to him, “The Lord your God declared that he would bring these disasters upon this place.”
The Lord did these things because you sinned against him and did not obey his voice.
“Look, I have now freed you from the bronze chains on your hands. If you think it is good to come with me to Babylon, then come, and I will not neglect you.

But if you think it is bad to come to Babylon, then turn back and go to Gedaliah son of Ahikam, son of Shaphan, whom the king of Babylon appointed in the land of Judah. Live with him among the people. Whatever you think is good to do, go and do it.” The captain of the guard gave him gifts and sent him
to Gedaliah son of Ahikam, at Mizpah. He lived among the people who remained in the land.

All the army commanders in the countryside, together with their men in the countryside, heard that the king of Babylon had appointed Gedaliah in the land and had entrusted to him men and their wives whom he had deported to Babylon.

Samael son of Nethaniah, Johanan son of Kareah, Seraiah son of Tanhumeth, the sons of Ephai, son of the Netophathite, and Jezaniah son of the Maacathite came to Gedaliah at Mizpah, together with their men.

Gedaliah swore an oath to them and their other men, saying to them, “Do not be afraid of the servants of the Chaldeans. Instead, live in this land and serve the king of Babylon, and things will go well for you.

Look, I am staying here before you at Mizpah to stand before the Chaldeans who come to you. As for you, gather wine, summer fruit, and oil, put them in your containers, and live in the cities you have taken over.”

All the Jews in the land of Moab, those in the land of the Ammonites, those in Edom, and those throughout the land heard that the king of Babylon had left a remnant of the people of Judah and had appointed Gedaliah son of Ahikam over them.
So the Jews returned from the places where they had been scattered. They came to the land of Judah, to Gedaliah at Mizpah, and gathered wine, a very large quantity of summer fruit, and oil.
Johanan son of Kareah and all the army commanders who were in the countryside came to Gedaliah at Mizpah.
They said to him, “Do you really know that Baalis, king of the Ammonites, has sent Ishmael son of Nethaniah to kill you?” But Gedaliah did not believe them.

Johanan said secretly to Gedaliah in Mizpah, “I will go now and strike down Ishmael. Do not let anyone know, lest he kill you and all the Jews gathered around you be scattered and the remnant of Judah perish.”
Gedaliah said to Johanan, “Do not do this, for you are speaking falsely about Ishmael.”
In the seventh month, Ishmael son of Nethaniah, son of Eleasah, who was of royal descent, came with ten men to Gedaliah at Mizpah. They ate bread together there.
Ishmael and the ten men with him rose up and struck Gedaliah with a sword—the man whom the king of Babylon had appointed over the land—
along with all the Jews who were with him in Mizpah and all the Chaldeans whom they found there.
On the second day after he had struck down Gedaliah, while no one knew about it,

men came from Shechem, Salem, and Samaria, eighty men with their beards shaved and their clothes torn, beating themselves in mourning. They carried grain offerings and frankincense to bring into the house of the Lord.
Ishmael came out from Mizpah to meet them. They were walking along weeping. He said to them, “Come in to Gedaliah.”
When they entered the middle of the city, Ishmael slaughtered them and threw them down into the cistern, he and those with him.
They found ten men there who said to Ishmael, “Do not kill us, for we have stores in the fields of wheat, barley, honey, and oil.” So he spared them and did not kill them along with their companions.
The cistern into which Ishmael threw all those he had killed was a large cistern that King Asa had made against [?], king of [?]. Ishmael filled it with the slain.

Ishmael carried off all the people who remained in Mizpah, along with the king’s children whom the chief of the guards had entrusted to Gedaliah son of Ahikam. Ishmael set out and went toward the land of the Ammonites.
Johanan son of Kareah and all the army commanders who were with him heard about all the evil Ishmael had done.
They took their entire army and went to fight him. They found him beside a large body of water at Gibeon.
When all the people who were with Ishmael saw Johanan and the army commanders with him, they rejoiced.
All the people turned back and went to Johanan.
But Ishmael fled with eight men and went to the Ammonites.

Johanan and all the army commanders with him took all the remaining people whom he had recovered from Ishmael: men strong in battle, women, the others, and the eunuchs. He brought them back from Gibeon.
They went and stayed at Gaberoth, in the land of Canaan, near Bethlehem, intending to go down to Egypt,
away from the Chaldeans, because they were afraid of them, since Ishmael had killed Gedaliah, whom the king of Babylon had appointed over the land.
All the army commanders came—Johanan and Azariah son of Josiah, son of Maaseiah—along with all the people, from the least to the greatest,
to Jeremiah the prophet. They said to him, “Please show us mercy and pray to the Lord your God for these who remain, for we have become few out of many, as your own eyes have seen.
Let the Lord your God tell us the way we should walk and what we should do.”
Jeremiah said to them, “I have heard you. I will pray to the Lord our God as you have asked. Whatever the Lord says, I will tell you; I will not hide any word from you.”
They in turn said to Jeremiah, “May the Lord be a true and trustworthy witness among us if we do not act according to all the words with which the Lord sends you to us.
Whether it is good or bad, we will obey the voice of the Lord our God, to whom we are sending you, so that things may go well for us, because we will obey the voice of the Lord our God.”
After ten days, the word of the Lord came to Jeremiah.
He called Johanan, the army commanders who were with him, and all the people, from the least to the greatest.
He said to them, “This is what the Lord has said:

“If you settle and remain in this land, I will build you up and establish you, and I will not tear you down. I will plant you and not uproot you, for I have relented over all the disasters I sent to bring upon you.”
‘Do not be afraid of the king of Babylon, whom you fear. Do not be afraid,’ says the Lord, ‘because I am with you to rescue you and save you from his hands.
I will grant you mercy, have mercy on you, and bring you back to your land.
But if you say, “We will not stay in this land,” refusing to obey the voice of the Lord,
and say, “We will go to the land of Egypt, where we will not see war, hear the sound of the trumpet, or go hungry for bread, but will settle there,”
then listen to the word of the Lord. This is what the Lord has said: If you set your faces toward Egypt and go to settle there,
the sword you fear will find you in the land of Egypt, and the famine you fear will overtake you in the land of Egypt, and you will die there.
Every person and every foreigner who has decided to settle in the land of Egypt will perish by the sword and famine. None of them will escape the disasters that I will bring upon them.

This is what the Lord has said: Just as my anger came upon those living in Jerusalem, so my anger will come upon you if you go to Egypt. You will become a desolation and become slaves, a curse, and an object of scorn. You will never see this place again.’
Because of what the Lord has said concerning you, survivors of Judah, do not go to Egypt. Now you will surely know
that you acted wickedly in your souls when you sent me before the Lord, saying, ‘Pray for us before the Lord our God, and we will do everything the Lord tells you.’
I told you, but you did not obey the voice of the Lord, with whose message he sent me to you.
So now you will perish by the sword and famine in the place where you want to go and live.”
When Jeremiah had finished speaking before all the people all these words of the Lord, which the Lord had sent to them,
Azariah son of Amasai, Johanan son of Kareah, and all the men said to Jeremiah, “You are lying! The Lord did not send you to us to say, ‘Do not go to Egypt to settle there.’
Instead, Baruch son of Neriah is making you say these things to us so that you can hand us over to the Chaldeans and they can kill us.”
Johanan, all the army commanders, and all the people did not obey the voice of the Lord by remaining in the land of Judah.
Then Johanan and all the army commanders took [?] all the rest of Judah’s survivors, whom they had turned away to keep them from settling in the land:
the men, the women, the little children, the king’s daughters, and the people whom Nebuzaradan had left behind with Gedaliah son of Ahikam, as well as Jeremiah the prophet and Baruch son of Neriah.
They went to the land of Egypt because they had not obeyed the voice of the Lord, and they arrived at Tahpanhes.
The word of the Lord came to Jeremiah in Tahpanhes, saying,
“Take some large stones and hide them at the entrance to the gateway of Pharaoh’s house in Tahpanhes, in the sight of the men of Judah.

Tell them, ‘This is what the Lord has said: Look, I will send and bring Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, and he will set his throne upon these stones that you have hidden, and he will raise his weapons.’

He will come in and strike the land of Egypt: those destined for death will go to death, those destined for deportation will be deported, and those destined for the sword will be handed over to the sword.
He will kindle a fire in the temples of its gods, burn them, and carry them away. He will strip the land of Egypt as a shepherd wraps himself in his garment, and he will leave in peace.
He will shatter the pillars of the city of the sun, which is On, and he will burn their houses with fire.
The word of the Lord that came to Jeremiah, to be spoken concerning all the Jews living in the land of Egypt, and those living in Migdol, Tahpanhes, and the land of Pathros, saying to them:
This is what the Lord, the God of [?], said: You have seen all the disasters that I brought upon Jerusalem and the cities of Judah. Look, they are deserted today, with no one living in them,
because of the wicked things they did to provoke me to anger, going to offer incense to other gods whom you did not know.
I sent my servants the prophets to you. I sent them early, saying, ‘Do not commit this foul deed that I hate.’
They did not listen to me or incline their ears to turn away from their wickedness and stop offering incense to other gods.
My anger came down, and my wrath blazed in the gates of Judah and outside Jerusalem. They became a wasteland, a place where no one walks, as they are today.

Now, therefore, this is what the Lord Almighty said: Why are you doing these great evils to yourselves, causing man and woman, young child and nursing infant to be killed from among Judah, so that none of you remains?

You provoke me to anger with the works of your hands, offering incense to other gods in the land of Egypt, where you have gone to live, so that you will be killed and become a curse and an object of scorn among the nations of the earth.

Have you forgotten the wicked deeds of your ancestors, the wicked deeds of the kings of Judah, the wicked deeds of your rulers, and the wicked deeds of your wives, which they committed in the land of Judah and outside Jerusalem?
They have not stopped these things to this day, nor have they kept my commands and my laws, which I set before you and before your ancestors.
Therefore, this is what the Lord said: Look, I will set my face
to destroy the entire remnant in Egypt. They will fall by the sword and perish from hunger, from the least to the greatest of them. They will become an object of scorn, a ruin, and a curse.
I will punish those living in the land of Egypt as I punished Jerusalem, with sword, hunger, and death.

No one from the remnant of Judah who lives as a foreigner in the land of Egypt will escape to return to the land of Judah, where they hope in their hearts to return. They will not return there, except those who escape.

All the men who knew that their wives offered incense to other gods, together with all the other women—a large assembly—and all the people living in the land of Egypt, in Pathros, answered Jeremiah, saying to him:
As for the word you have spoken to us in the Lord’s name, we will not listen to you about it.

We will certainly carry out every word that comes from our mouths: we will offer sacrifices to the Queen of Heaven and pour out drink offerings to her, just as we, our ancestors, our kings, and our rulers did in the cities of Judah and outside Jerusalem. We had our fill of bread, lived securely, and saw no disaster.
But when we stopped offering sacrifices to the Queen of Heaven, we all suffered want and perished by the sword and famine.
So we will offer incense to the Queen of Heaven and pour out drink offerings to her. Was it without our husbands’ knowledge that we made cakes for her and poured out wine to her?
Jeremiah spoke to all the powerful men and to the women of all the people who had answered him with these words, saying to them:

“Was it not the sacrifice that you offered in the cities of Judah and the streets of Jerusalem—you, your ancestors, your kings, your officials, and the people of the land—that the Lord remembered and that came into his mind?”
The Lord could no longer endure the wickedness of your deeds. Because of the detestable things you did, your land became a wasteland, a place where no one walks, and a curse, as it is today.
Before those to whom you offer incense and among whom you sinned against the Lord, you did not obey the Lord or follow his commands, his law, and his decrees. All these disasters have come upon you.
And Jeremiah said to all the people and to the women, “Listen to the word of the Lord.

This is what the Lord, the God of [?], said: ‘You and your wives spoke with your mouths and carried it out with your hands, saying, “We will certainly fulfill the vows we made to offer sacrifices to the Queen of Heaven and pour out wine offerings to her.” You have firmly held to your vows and have indeed carried them out.’

Therefore listen to the word of the Lord, all you people of Judah who live in the land of Egypt: ‘Look, I have sworn by my great name,’ says the Lord, ‘that from now on my name will no longer be on the lips of any of the people of Judah throughout the land of Egypt, saying, “As the Lord, the Lord, lives.”
Look, I am watching over them to afflict them, not to do them good. All the people of Judah who live in the land of Egypt will perish by the sword and famine until they are destroyed.

Those who escape the sword will return from the land of Egypt to the land of Judah, few in number. All the survivors of Judah who became foreigners in the land of Egypt will know whose word stands—mine or theirs.
And this will be a sign to you that I myself will visit you with disasters,’ says the Lord.

This is what the Lord said: ‘Look, I will hand over Hophra, king of Egypt, to his enemy and to those who seek his life, just as I handed over Zedekiah, king of Judah, to Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, his enemy, who sought his life.’”
The word that Jeremiah the prophet spoke to Baruch son of Neriah when he wrote these words in a book as Jeremiah dictated them, in the fourth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah:
This is what the Lord, the God of [?], said concerning you, Baruch:
“You said, ‘Woe to me! Woe to me! The Lord has added suffering to my sorrow. I lay down amid sighs and found no rest.’
Tell him this: ‘This is what the Lord said: Look, what I have built I will tear down, and what I have planted I will uproot.
And you are seeking great things for yourself! Do not seek them, for look, I will bring disasters upon all humanity,’ says the Lord. ‘But I will let you escape with your life wherever you go.’
Zedekiah was twenty-one years old when he became king, and he reigned for eleven years. His mother’s name was Hamutal, daughter of Jeremiah from Libnah.

In the ninth year of his reign, in the ninth month, on the tenth day of the month, Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, came with his entire army against Jerusalem. They surrounded it and built a wall against it, with four [?] of stone all around.
The city remained under siege until the eleventh year of King Zedekiah.
On the ninth day of the month, the famine became severe in the city, and there was no bread for the people of the land.

The city was breached, and all the fighting men fled. They left the city at night by the road through the gate between the wall and the outer wall, near the king’s garden. The Chaldeans were surrounding the city, and the men went along the road toward the Arabah.
The Chaldean army pursued the king near Jericho, and all his servants scattered away from him.
They captured the king and brought him to the king of Babylon at Riblah, and he pronounced judgment on him.
The king of Babylon slaughtered Zedekiah’s sons before his eyes, and he slaughtered all the officials of Judah at Riblah.
But he blinded Zedekiah’s eyes and bound him in fetters. The king of Babylon brought him to Babylon and had him confined in the mill house until the day he died.
And in the fifth month, on the tenth day of the month, Nebuzaradan, the commander of the guard, who served before the king of Babylon, came to Jerusalem.
He burned the house of the Lord, the king’s house, and all the houses of the city. He burned every large house with fire.
And the whole army of the Chaldeans that was with the commander of the guard demolished every wall surrounding Jerusalem.
And Nebuzaradan left the remaining people as vine growers and farmers.
And the Chaldeans broke up the bronze pillars in the house of the Lord, the stands, and the bronze Sea in the house of the Lord, and carried their bronze to Babylon.
And the crown, the bowls, the meat hooks, and all the bronze utensils used in the service,
along with the censers, the lampstands, the incense bowls, and the cups—the vessels made of gold were all gold, and those made of silver were all silver—the commander of the guard took them.
And the two pillars, the Sea, and the twelve bronze oxen beneath the Sea, which King Solomon had made to place in the house of the Lord—their bronze was beyond measure.
And the pillars were each eighteen cubits high. A cord twelve cubits long measured the circumference of each, and its thickness was four fingers all around.

There was a bronze capital on top of them, and the capital was five cubits high. A network of chains and rows of pomegranates surrounded the capital; they were all bronze. The second pillar had the same features, with eight pomegranates to each cubit of the twelve cubits.
There were ninety-six pomegranates on one side, and all the pomegranates on the chainwork around it numbered one hundred.
And the commander of the guard took Seraiah the chief priest, Zephaniah the second priest, and the three who guarded the entrance,

along with a eunuch who supervised the fighting men, seven men who were prominent in the king’s presence and were found in the city, the army’s secretary who registered the people of the land, and sixty men from among the people of the land who were found in the middle of the city.
Nebuzaradan, the commander of the guard, took them and brought them to the king of Babylon at Riblah,
in the land of Hamath.

And in the thirty-seventh year after Jehoiakim king of Judah had been deported, in the twelfth month, on the twenty-fourth day of the month, Evil-merodach king of Babylon, in the year he became king, lifted up the head of Jehoiakim king of Judah and brought him out of the house where he was held under guard.
He spoke kindly to him and placed his throne above the thrones of the kings who were with him in Babylon.
And he changed the clothes he had worn in prison, and they put other clothes on him. He regularly ate his bread in the king’s presence throughout all the days of his life.
And the allowance assigned to him by the king of Babylon was regularly given to him, day by day, until the day he died, throughout all the days of his life.
